subject: Audit logs evidence request & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Audit logs evidence request & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call with FinCo InfoSec: 

What you asked for:
- Access audit logs that show who accessed PII and when (user identity, timestamp, action, resource).
- Exportable evidence for SOC 2: both raw logs (CSV/JSON) and a human-readable summary report.
- Confirmation of retention and export options (how long logs are kept, export formats, immutable checksums).
- Data residency and whether log storage/exports can be limited to US infrastructure.

Our proposed next steps:
1) We'll provide a sample CSV export (fields & one-week sample) and the audit log schema by EOD tomorrow (Feb 19). (Dev will own.)
2) Tech deep-dive with Dev & your engineers to confirm field mappings, export method (S3/GCS/presigned link) and retention SLAs — propose Feb 19 at 10:00 AM PT.
3) We'll include a short note on our retention policy (default/extended) and options for dedicated retention on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Attachments: we'll attach a sample CSV and a short audit spec PDF.

Open questions we flagged on the call you may want to confirm before the tech call:
- Time window required for exports for the SOC 2 audit (12 months vs 24 months vs 7 years).
- Whether you need daily recurring exports during the audit window or a one-off export.
- Need for immutable checksums (SHA256) on exports for chain-of-custody.

If that aligns, we'll move forward with the sample artifacts and lock the tech call on Feb 19 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- For the SOC 2 evidence we need both the raw audit log exports and a short human-readable summary that shows: count of PII reads by user, top users by access volume, and export of any bulk-download events.
- Preferred export format: CSV for the raw log (we ingest into our SIEM) and PDF/HTML for the summary.
- Time window: for the initial evidence deliverable we need prior 12 months, but the auditor may ask for up to 3 years—can you confirm retention policy and whether extended retention (up to 7 years) is available under an enterprise commit?
- We expect the export to include an immutable checksum and a mapping of acted_by -> SSO user id.

Confirming the Feb 19 10:00 AM PT tech call works for us. Please include meeting dial-in and your engineer who can show a sample export.

—Peter

Subject: Audit log sample & schema (finco_audit_sample.csv, redwood_audit_spec.pdf)

Hi Peter / Asha — attaching a short one-week sample export (finco_audit_sample.csv) and the spec (redwood_audit_spec.pdf). Below is a quick summary of the schema and export options so you can share with your auditor ahead of the call.

Sample schema (columns in CSV):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- acted_by (SSO user id/email)
- action (read, write, delete, export, config_change)
- resource_id (document/file id)
- resource_type (document, model, embedding)
- fields_accessed (comma-separated list of fields, flagged if PII)
- ip_address
- user_agent
- request_id
- outcome (success/failure)

Export methods supported:
- Ad-hoc CSV: generate and deliver via presigned S3 URL (HTTPS).
- Scheduled exports: daily/weekly to customer-owned S3 bucket (AWS role assumption).
- Direct SIEM push: syslog/HTTPS webhook (usually via partner connector).

Retention windows:
- Hosted default: full audit logs retained for 90 days online, 12 months archived hot storage.
- Extended retention: up to 7 years via Dedicated/Private deployments or add-on archival for enterprise customers (requires contract).

Access controls and evidence:
- Role-based access: only users with "auditor" or "admin" roles can request exports.
- Exports include SHA256 checksum file alongside CSV when requested to support chain-of-custody.
- We can include mapping tables to map acted_by -> SSO user directory id in the CSV.

Data residency:
- Audit logs are stored in region-specific storage: US (default) and EU (by request). If you need US-only residency, we can ensure exports and storage stay in US datacenters under our Hosted/Private options.

If you want, I can paste a 10-row sample inline in the call — otherwise the attached CSV has the snippet. Looking forward to the call tomorrow.

- Dev

Thanks Dev — received the files and the summary. A couple of last clarifications before the call: 
1) Confirm exports will include SHA256 checksum files next to the CSVs (for chain-of-custody).
2) Confirm that acted_by will contain a stable SSO identifier we can map to our directory (not just display name).
3) For the human-readable summary, can you include a pre-built pivot that highlights PII read events (fields flagged as PII) and a per-user count? That helps accelerate the auditor review.

If you can confirm 1–3, we're good for the tech call at 10:00 AM PT. Also please include a short checklist for what we should have on the call (e.g., access to S3 bucket, sample user IDs).

Regards,
Peter
